description: Average the customer counts over every employee, with employees who have no customers counted as zero.

c.request: On average, how many customers does each support rep look after? Don't round. Average the customer counts over every employee, with employees who have no customers counted as zero.
c.sql: SELECT AVG(customer_count) FROM (SELECT e.EmployeeId, COUNT(c.CustomerId) as customer_count FROM Employee e LEFT JOIN Customer c ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId) as customer_counts

a.request: Counting, for every employee, the customers whose `SupportRepId` is that employee (zero for employees with none), what is the average number of customers per employee? Don't round.
a.sql: SELECT AVG(customer_count) FROM (SELECT e.EmployeeId, COUNT(c.CustomerId) as customer_count FROM Employee e LEFT JOIN Customer c ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId) as employee_customer_counts

d.request: The average customer count per employee across all employees, with employees having no customers counted as zero.
d.sql: SELECT AVG(customer_count) as average_customer_count FROM (SELECT e.EmployeeId, COUNT(c.CustomerId) as customer_count FROM Employee e LEFT JOIN Customer c ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId) as employee_customer_counts

b.request: The average number of customers each employee supports, including employees with no customers assigned.
b.sql: SELECT AVG(customer_count) as average_customers_per_employee FROM (SELECT e.EmployeeId, COUNT(c.CustomerId) as customer_count FROM Employee e LEFT JOIN Customer c ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId) as employee_customer_counts
b.raw: The average number of customers each employee supports, including employees with no customers assigned.
